data.statement: Resolve Gitea issue #36 by removing the dead legacy state-file layer from deterministic and AI chunking without changing runtime behavior, while preserving #31's live throttling helpers and explicitly resolving the production-dead semantic-cut helpers.

acceptance: deterministic_chunking_service no longer defines load_chunking_report, _load_partial_chunks, _load_resume_state, _write_running_state, _persist_terminal_state, _build_operation_state, or _write_chunk_payload, and their unused imports are removed.

The live _CHECKPOINT_PARAGRAPH_INTERVAL, _CHECKPOINT_TIME_INTERVAL_SECONDS, _PROGRESS_EMIT_INTERVAL_SECONDS, _should_write_checkpoint, and _should_emit_progress implementation and tests remain unchanged and green.

ai_chunking_service no longer defines the legacy _load_resume_state, _compute_input_fingerprint, _resolve_additional_chunking_instructions, _build_profile_runtime_metadata, _restore_descriptor_resume_state, _restore_profile_usage_history, _merge_profile_usage_history, _validate_chunk_descriptors, _write_descriptor_state, _build_operation_state, or _write_chunk_payload chain, and import fallout is pruned without removing build_operation_output_path.

Descriptor contract tests exercise _validate_chunk_descriptor_prefix directly for complete and invalid-prefix semantics, and resume fixtures use chunking_document_service.source_fingerprint rather than the deleted wrapper.

A red-first single-document contract check proves the retired legacy helper names are absent from both chunking service modules while canonical chunks_text.json checkpoint, resume, cancellation, failure, and completion behavior remains green.

The existing obsolete-sidecar durable requirement is reconciled to cover both chunking services using only canonical document persistence and links to the exact regression check without creating a duplicate requirement.

If the recommended owner decision is approved, semantic_cut_priority and split_for_hard_limit remain as reference implementations, REQ-FUNC-747584c1-19b0-42eb-8ba0-efb89579bd88 and REQ-FUNC-11c404c6-4de0-47d9-b539-8de5a7f76a02 become Planned, and the spec/component documentation no longer presents their unintegrated behavior as active runtime behavior.
No Text Chunking runtime output, strict document field, checkpoint cadence, progress cadence, resume boundary, or downstream behavior changes.
Focused Chunking tests, the complete pytest and Ruff gates, traceability audit, coverage audit, and changed-set impact complete without blocking findings.
assumptions: Exact source-and-test reference scans are authoritative for the listed deletion candidates; dynamic string-based invocation is not part of the project contract.
The #31 checkpoint and progress helpers/constants are live production behavior and are excluded from deletion.
Cross-module private helpers _build_paragraph_records, _build_chunking_warnings, and _chapter_count_from_chunks remain unchanged; promoting them to public APIs would add unnecessary scope.
open_questions: Should #36 retain semantic_cut_priority and split_for_hard_limit as planned reference implementations, reclassify their two currently Active requirements as Planned, and correct the spec/component documentation instead of deleting the helpers and their tests?
data.reason: The dead sidecar deletions are mechanically bounded, but changing or deleting code tied to two Active product requirements is an owner-level contract decision. Pausing prevents either silently erasing intended future behavior or continuing to present unintegrated helpers as implemented runtime behavior.
recommended_responses: Yes. Retain both helpers, mark the two contracts Planned, and document that production integration needs a separately approved follow-up; do not create a Gitea follow-up issue until separately authorized.
scope: In scope: delete the zero-production-reference deterministic and AI legacy sidecar/resume helpers listed by #36; prune import fallout; preserve #31 checkpoint/progress throttling; repoint obsolete tests to canonical descriptor-prefix and fingerprint APIs; add a red-first contract check preventing legacy helper reintroduction; reconcile the obsolete-sidecar requirement; and, if approved, retain semantic_cut_priority and split_for_hard_limit as planned reference implementations while correcting their requirements/spec/component documentation. Out of scope: runtime chunking semantics, checkpoint cadence, document schema, public renaming of cross-module private helpers, tickets #37/#38, creating or commenting on Gitea issues without separate approval, and delivery operations.
